metadata.archetype_justification: The application has a database connection (SQL Server via SqlConnection) with both read (SELECT) and write (INSERT) operations against a timesheets table. It manages user-specific data (employee_id-scoped entries). This matches the stateful-crud archetype.

classification_consistency_check.reason: Score 1.09 < 1.5 yields Not Ready band but 8 High findings maps to 2-11 High → Remediation Required rule. Adopting Not Ready as authoritative because the overall score is below 1.5 and every category scores below 1.5, indicating systemic unreadiness across all dimensions rather than targeted gaps that could be remediated incrementally.

top_gaps.title: Infrastructure as Code Coverage
top_gaps.gap: No IaC exists — all infrastructure is manually provisioned
top_gaps.impact: Cannot reproduce environment; disaster recovery impossible; no audit trail for changes

top_gaps.title: CI/CD Automation
top_gaps.gap: No CI/CD pipeline — deployment is manual VS publish to network share
top_gaps.impact: No quality gates, no automated testing, high risk of human error on every deploy

top_gaps.title: Secrets Management
top_gaps.gap: Plaintext SQL Server credentials in web.config committed to git
top_gaps.impact: Credential exposure; no rotation; anyone with repo access has DB credentials

top_gaps.title: Monolith vs Microservices
top_gaps.gap: Single tightly-coupled WebForms page with no module boundaries
top_gaps.impact: Cannot scale independently; no team autonomy; deployment is all-or-nothing

findings.title: Managed Compute — all compute on-premises IIS 6
findings.description: All compute is on a single on-premises IIS 6 server running Windows Server 2003. No AWS compute resources are defined.
findings.gap: No managed compute — application runs on end-of-life on-premises infrastructure with no cloud presence.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to managed compute on AWS. AWS Lambda with API Gateway or ECS Fargate are appropriate targets for this small application.

findings.title: Managed Databases — self-managed SQL Server 2005 on-premises
findings.description: Database is self-managed SQL Server 2005 on-premises at IP 10.0.6.15. No managed database service configured.
findings.gap: All database operations against a self-managed, on-premises SQL Server 2005 instance with no automated patching, backup, failover, or scaling.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to Amazon RDS for SQL Server or Aurora PostgreSQL. Use AWS DMS for data migration.

findings.title: Workflow Orchestration — no orchestration or error handling
findings.description: No workflow orchestration service in use. Write operations are hardcoded in a single method with no error handling, validation, or retry logic.
findings.gap: No orchestration — all workflow logic hardcoded with no error handling or retry capability.
findings.recommendation: Implement structured error handling and validation in the application layer. For a simple CRUD service, a full orchestration service is not needed initially.

findings.title: Async Messaging — no messaging infrastructure
findings.description: No messaging or streaming infrastructure. For a stateful-crud service, state changes cannot be propagated to downstream systems without tight synchronous coupling.
findings.gap: No messaging where state changes cross service boundaries — tight coupling required for any integration.
findings.recommendation: Implement event publishing on state changes (SNS or EventBridge) when modernizing to enable decoupled downstream integration.

findings.title: Network Security — no VPC or network segmentation
findings.description: No network security configuration. Application and database communicate over unencrypted, unsegmented network. Forms auth cookie without SSL.
findings.gap: No VPC, no security groups, no network segmentation. No SSL enforcement.
findings.recommendation: Deploy in a VPC with private subnets for database, public subnets behind ALB for application. Enforce HTTPS.

findings.title: API Entry Point — no gateway or load balancer
findings.description: No API Gateway, ALB, CloudFront, or managed entry point. Application served directly from IIS 6.
findings.gap: Services exposed directly with no gateway, throttling, or centralized auth.
findings.recommendation: Place an API Gateway or ALB in front of the application with throttling and authentication.

findings.title: Auto-Scaling — no scaling capability
findings.description: No auto-scaling. Application runs on a single IIS server with no ability to scale in response to load.
findings.gap: No auto-scaling — all capacity statically provisioned on a single server.
findings.recommendation: Configure auto-scaling appropriate to the target platform (ECS service auto-scaling, Lambda concurrency).

findings.title: Backup and Recovery — no backup configuration
findings.description: No backup configuration in the repository. No automated backups, no retention policies, no restore procedures documented.
findings.gap: No backup configuration found — no automated backups, no retention policy, no restore procedures.
findings.recommendation: Enable automated backups with defined retention on RDS/Aurora. Enable PITR. Document and test restore procedures.

findings.title: Infrastructure as Code Coverage — zero IaC
findings.description: Zero IaC coverage. No Terraform, CloudFormation, CDK, or any IaC tool present. All infrastructure manually provisioned.
findings.gap: No IaC — 100% of infrastructure manually created. Environment cannot be reproduced.
findings.recommendation: Define all infrastructure in IaC (CDK or Terraform). Start with target-state architecture: VPC, compute, database, monitoring.

findings.title: CI/CD Automation — no pipeline exists
findings.description: No CI/CD pipeline. Deployment is manual publish from Visual Studio 2005 to a network share.
findings.gap: No CI/CD — all deployments manual with no quality gates or automated testing.
findings.recommendation: Implement CI/CD pipeline: source trigger → build → test → deploy staging → integration test → deploy production.

findings.title: Programming Languages — VB.NET on .NET Framework 2.0 (EOL)
findings.description: VB.NET targeting .NET Framework 2.0 with ASP.NET WebForms. All three axes (language version, framework, SDK) are end-of-life or deprecated.
findings.gap: Compound legacy: VB.NET + .NET Framework 2.0 + WebForms — no AWS SDK support, no cloud-native tooling at this version.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite in C# targeting .NET 8+ with ASP.NET Core. Provides full AWS SDK v3 support and cloud-native tooling.

findings.title: Monolith vs Microservices — tightly-coupled single-page monolith
findings.description: Tightly-coupled monolith with no module boundaries. Single WebForms page with inline SQL, InProc session, ViewState. No separation of concerns.
findings.gap: Tightly-coupled monolith with pervasive shared state and no architectural boundaries.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite with clear architectural boundaries: repository pattern, service layer, API/presentation separation. See Decomposition Strategy.

findings.title: Async vs Sync Communication — primarily synchronous
findings.description: All communication is synchronous WebForms postback. For stateful-crud, some async for cross-service state propagation is expected. No async capability exists.
findings.gap: Primarily synchronous with no async patterns for future integration.
findings.recommendation: Implement event publishing on state changes (EventBridge) when modernizing for decoupled downstream integration.

findings.title: Long-Running Process Handling — all operations synchronous
findings.description: All operations synchronous with no timeout or async handling. No command timeouts, no async patterns, no background work capability.
findings.gap: All operations synchronous regardless of duration — no protection against long-running queries.
findings.recommendation: Set command timeouts. Implement async/await in the modernized version. Use async jobs with status polling for batch operations.

findings.title: API Versioning — no API or versioning
findings.description: No API versioning. Application is a WebForms page with postback, not a versioned API. No mechanism for backward-compatible evolution.
findings.gap: No versioning — no structured API exists. Changes affect all users immediately.
findings.recommendation: Implement URL-path versioning (e.g., /api/v1/timesheets) from day one in the rewrite. Define API contracts with OpenAPI.

findings.title: Service Discovery — hard-coded IP address
findings.description: No service discovery. Database endpoint is hard-coded as IP 10.0.6.15 in web.config. No DNS abstraction or dynamic discovery.
findings.gap: All service endpoints hard-coded as literal IP addresses.
findings.recommendation: Use RDS endpoints (DNS) instead of IPs. For inter-service communication, use AWS Cloud Map or environment variables with parameter store.

findings.title: Unstructured Data Storage — no managed object storage
findings.description: No unstructured data storage configured. No S3 buckets, no document storage, no file handling capabilities.
findings.gap: No managed object storage for unstructured data.
findings.recommendation: If timesheet documents are needed, implement S3 storage with lifecycle policies. Consider Textract for paper timesheet digitization.

findings.title: Unified Data Access Layer — queries scattered in UI code
findings.description: Database queries scattered directly in UI event handlers. SqlConnection and raw SQL used in Page_Load and button click handlers with no abstraction.
findings.gap: Database imports and queries scattered in UI code with no pattern. Business logic and data access interleaved.
findings.recommendation: Implement repository/service layer pattern. Use ORM (EF Core, Dapper) or dedicated data access class with parameterized queries.

findings.title: Database Engine Version — SQL Server 2005 (EOL 10+ years)
findings.description: SQL Server 2005, end of extended support April 2016. Unsupported for over 10 years. No security patches available.
findings.gap: Database engine past EOL by 10+ years. No version pinning in IaC. Critical security risk.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to supported engine immediately: RDS SQL Server 2019/2022 or Aurora PostgreSQL. Use AWS DMS.

findings.title: Stored Procedures — inline SQL with string concatenation
findings.description: No stored procedures visible in repo. All SQL is inline with string concatenation. SQL is simple ANSI-compatible but creates injection risk and engine coupling.
findings.gap: Inline SQL with string concatenation creates SQL injection risk. Database may have server-side objects not visible in repo.
findings.recommendation: Convert all inline SQL to parameterized queries. Audit SQL Server instance for stored procedures/triggers. Plan extraction if found.

findings.title: Encryption at Rest — no encryption configured
findings.description: No encryption at rest. SQL Server 2005 does not support TDE. Employee data stored unencrypted.
findings.gap: No encryption at rest. Sensitive employee data unencrypted on EOL engine without TDE support.
findings.recommendation: Enable encryption at rest with KMS when migrating to RDS/Aurora.

findings.title: API Authentication — forms auth without SSL
findings.description: Forms authentication with requireSSL=false. Auth cookie transmitted in cleartext. No token-based auth (OAuth2/JWT).
findings.gap: No token-based authentication. Forms auth cookie without SSL. Vulnerable to session hijacking.
findings.recommendation: Implement OAuth2/JWT with managed IdP (Cognito). Enforce HTTPS. Use API Gateway authorizers.

findings.title: Centralized Identity — local forms auth only
findings.description: Application manages own authentication via ASP.NET Forms auth. No external IdP, no OIDC/SAML, no SSO.
findings.gap: Application manages own authentication with no external IdP integration or SSO.
findings.recommendation: Integrate with centralized IdP (Amazon Cognito or corporate IdP via OIDC/SAML). Enable SSO.

findings.title: Secrets Management — plaintext credentials in git
findings.description: Plaintext database credentials committed to repository: User ID=ts_app;Password=Time2006! in web.config.
findings.gap: Plaintext credentials in version-controlled source. Critical security risk — all repo readers have DB credentials.
findings.recommendation: Immediately remove plaintext credentials and rotate password. Store all secrets in AWS Secrets Manager with automated rotation.

findings.title: Compute Hardening — EOL OS, no patching possible
findings.description: Windows Server 2003 and IIS 6 are EOL and cannot receive security patches. Debug mode enabled in production.
findings.gap: Running on EOL OS that cannot be patched. No vulnerability scanning. Debug mode enabled.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to supported OS. Use managed compute (Fargate/Lambda) to eliminate OS patching. Disable debug in production.

findings.title: Application Security Pipeline — no scanning tools
findings.description: No SAST, DAST, or dependency scanning. No CI/CD pipeline to integrate into. Known SQL injection vulnerability undetected.
findings.gap: No security scanning tools. Known vulnerabilities (SQL injection) remain undetected by automated tooling.
findings.recommendation: Integrate SAST (SonarQube, Semgrep) and dependency scanning into CI/CD from day one.

findings.title: Distributed Tracing — no tracing instrumented
findings.description: No distributed tracing. No X-Ray, OpenTelemetry, or trace propagation. No request-level visibility.
findings.gap: No tracing — no request-level visibility, no database call timing, no error correlation.
findings.recommendation: Instrument with OpenTelemetry or AWS X-Ray. Trace HTTP requests and database calls.

findings.title: SLO Definitions — no SLOs defined
findings.description: No SLOs defined. No CloudWatch alarms, no latency targets, no error rate thresholds, no availability targets.
findings.gap: No SLOs — no formal definition of acceptable service levels.
findings.recommendation: Define SLOs: availability (99.9%), latency p99 (<500ms), error rate (<0.1%). Implement CloudWatch alarms.

findings.title: Business Metrics — no custom metrics
findings.description: No custom metrics published. No business event tracking or metrics instrumentation.
findings.gap: No custom metrics — no business outcome measurement capability.
findings.recommendation: Publish business metrics: timesheet submissions/hour, unique employees/day, peak submission windows.

findings.title: Anomaly Detection — no alerting configured
findings.description: No alerting. No CloudWatch alarms, no anomaly detection, no on-call integration.
findings.gap: No alerting — no way to detect degradation or failures without manual checking.
findings.recommendation: Configure CloudWatch alarms on error rates and latency. Enable anomaly detection. Integrate with on-call system.

findings.title: Integration Testing — no tests exist
findings.description: No tests of any kind — no unit tests, no integration tests, no test framework. Zero automated test coverage.
findings.gap: No integration tests — no automated tests at all. Changes cannot be validated without manual testing.
findings.recommendation: Implement integration tests from day one in the rewrite. Test CRUD operations, auth flows. Use xUnit for .NET.

findings.title: Incident Response — no runbooks or automation
findings.description: No incident response automation. No runbooks, no SSM Automation, no self-healing patterns.
findings.gap: No runbooks — incident response is entirely ad hoc.
findings.recommendation: Create runbooks for common failure scenarios. Start with documented procedures, progress to SSM Automation.

findings.title: Observability Ownership — no observability exists
findings.description: No observability ownership. No CODEOWNERS, no dashboards, no alarms with owners, no SLO attribution.
findings.gap: No observability ownership — no monitoring exists to own.
findings.recommendation: Define clear ownership: team-attributed dashboards, named alarm owners, SLO definitions with responsible teams.

findings.title: Resource Tagging — no AWS resources defined
findings.description: No resource tagging. No AWS resources defined in IaC. No tagging standard or enforcement.
findings.gap: No tags — no AWS resources defined. No tagging standard.
findings.recommendation: Implement tagging standard from day one: Environment, Team, CostCenter, Application, Service. Use Terraform default_tags or CDK Aspects.
